text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Monday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Twenty seven parties and political organisations intend to participate in the October 20 parliamentary elections. There are more than a 1,000 candidates for 141 seats.

- U.S. state officials did not succeed in persuading Lithuanian diplomats on Saturday that the 'Baltic Action Plan' is not an alternative to membership of the three Baltic countries in NATO. Lithuanian diplomats said it was not the right time for this initiative.

- A record prize of more than 579 million litas in the Golden pot of the Teleloto lottery was won on Sunday night. An opinion poll showed the popular game shown on commercial channel LNK attracts 21 percent of the population.

- Although there have been six governments in Lithuania since independence was regained in 1990, the problem of recovering diplomatic missions in Paris and Rome which it says were illegally occupied by Russia remain unsolved and Vilnius has not made much of an effort to settle the matter.

- The second $430,000 container for storing nuclear waste produced by German company GNB arrived at the Ignalina nuclear plant. Lithuania has signed a contract for 20 containers of this type for delivery by summer 1997.

- Latvian Prime Minister Andris Shkele will suggest to the Latvian parliament that it ratify the agreements with oil firms Amoco and Swedish Olje Prospektering only when he receives Lithuania's answer to his suggestion to settle the two countries' border dispute, which he put forward on September 9 in Nica. An answer is expected before September 18.

- Several cadidates to parliament acknowledged their former cooperation with foreign intelligence services in their central election commission questionnaires. The election law does not restrict participation of such people in the elections.
